mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate slower economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.3pp in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over the last quarter signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of quarters where GDPC1 declined.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in the last month, it signals a tight labor market with strong demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate robust economic growth.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200k in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increased by more than 200k in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% within the last two months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate a broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where HOUST decreased by more than 10% in the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals inflationary pressure combined with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real final sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% within the last month signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% in the last month.
